text:
Something has to give in Anaheim. Both teams have won five straight, and they've done it in opposite ways.

The Ducks' run belongs to Cutter Gauthier. He has goals in six straight games, 13 in all, and three hat tricks in his last five. Anaheim has scored 26 goals in those five wins on chances worth about 17, which is a heater by any definition, and the Ducks' 45% share of five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) on the season says the defense hasn't changed much. Mikael Granlund has 12 points in a six-game streak and Beckett Sennecke ten in four, so it isn't only Gauthier. But they take 5.2 penalties a game, the most in this matchup by a wide margin, and that bill comes due eventually. Laurent Brossoit starts, and Daily Faceoff reports coach Joel Quenneville expects Troy Terry to "likely" make his season debut.

Nashville's streak has more under it: 18-8 in goals and 55% of the chances. Juuse Saros stopped all 30 shots in Los Angeles last night, and the Predators are on the second night of a back-to-back with Justus Annunen (.873 in four games) in net, which our numbers count against them. The roster has turned over mid-run. Matthew Wood went to Seattle for Shane Wright, and Wright stepped straight onto Filip Forsberg's line with Jonathan Marchessault hurt. Steven Stamkos just passed into the all-time top five in power-play goals. Roman Josi is one point from 800 for his career, which is a strange week to also be reading your name in Edmonton trade rumors.

Our numbers have it close, Anaheim 3.3 expected goals to Nashville's 3.1, with two backup goalies who have combined for eight starts. Ross Colton is our depth sleeper on a Ducks defense that gives up the fifth-most chances in the league.
headline: Two five-game streaks, and only one is real

hunch.text: Two hot teams, two goalies who haven't played much, a Ducks team that takes penalties and a Predators team on tired legs. Our gut says this one gets loud.
